The problem here is you have a bunch of people all talking about something they know nothing about. Most of these are 2nd and 3rd hand stories. For example, if you work for a dealership, all of your training is paid for. You actually get paid to go to school. People that are dumb enough to go to trade school and pay all that money for absolutely nothing, should have done a little more research. Or that Ford tech about 8 minutes in with the heater core. I work for Ford, and there's a few people like me who know that once you do the same exact job a bunch of times, you get very fast without sacrificing quality. Everyone does the job one or two times and cries because it took all day. On an F150 it doesn't take me anywhere near 5 hours to replace one. Also, he never took the time to learn how to use Fords billing system. He should be getting more than 4.9, but he has no idea how to bill for it. You don't need 20k+ in tools, especially if you are just starting out. No one forces these kids that are very new to go out and buy a 10k tool box from SnapOn. Thats a choice. You can get something for under 1k that will last you quite a while. 

On this topic, there's more misinformation than good. Everyone has their stories. Most people can't think outside of themselves. They have expeiance doing one thing, or working for one place, and that's the standard set for everyone. They didn't make good money working for Ford, therefore no one can.

Any kind of manual labor work at 35-50hrs a week, especially in various weather situations (like some of these mechanics may not work in climate controlled facilities), is tough. Try working 40 hours in 90+ degree heat for 12-14 weeks in the South. It wastes you. And you're not getting paid a living wage. Different trade, but I feel for these guys. I have a couple of friends who are pretty decent mechanics but they don't really enjoy it, though it pays their bills and then some.

comments.text: Went to school for auto/diesel tech and early on one of my instructors pointed at a brand advertisement on the wall of a heavy duty truck towing a boat and said “they charge 150/hr and pay you 30/hr so they can have that while you pay rent” I still went into the industry anyways and can confirm even the spin off industries are like that but you can make a living in a way that does benefit you if you choose the right path. It’s not all dead ends but it’s also not a fantastic industry for everybody.
